document.title: SRS: ACME elevator FAMILY model
document.text:
# 1 Introduction
## 1.1 Purpose
This SRS specifies the software requirements for the ACME FAMILY elevator controller (hereafter, the system) for development. It is intended for ACME software engineers who will design and implement the controller, and for the development team for the alarm and emergency phone.
## 1.2 Scope
The FAMILY controller is used by adults and children, including people with reduced mobility who cannot use the stairs.
The system handles floor requests from the cabin and landings, cabin movement (with a rated load of 300 kg), door operation, and the cabin light.
The system does not handle the alarm or the emergency phone, which are independent devices with their own hardware and software.
## 1.3 Product Overview
### 1.3.1 Product perspective
The system has the following interfaces.
- Cabin panel (floor and alarm buttons), see [REF-02]. - Landing panels (call buttons), see [REF-02]. - Door sensors and door drive, see [REF-03]. - Motor drive (VFD), see [REF-03]. - Cabin light, see [REF-04].
### 1.3.3 User characteristics
Passengers are not expected to have any technical knowledge. Therefore, the user interface shall be similar to that of other elevators, with buttons for each floor and an alarm button. Children are not expected to use the elevator without adult supervision.
### 1.3.4 Limitations
The elevator must comply with the safety regulations listed in [REF-01].
## 1.5 SRS Overview
This SRS follows the outline of ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018. The sections of the outline that do not appear have been omitted for simplicity; notice that this reason is valid only in the framework of this academic course. Requirements are identified as FUN(xx) for functional, PER(xx) for performance, and QUA(xx) for quality requirements. Each requirement is a singular sentence that uses the verb "shall".
# 2 References
[REF-01] Applicable elevator safety regulations.
[REF-02] ACME FAMILY Panel Interface Specification, version 1.0, ACME Engineering, 2024.
[REF-03] ACME FAMILY Door and Motor Drive Interface Specification, version 1.1, ACME Engineering, 2024.
# 3 Specific requirements
## 3.1 Functions
FUN(01) When a passenger presses a floor button on the cabin panel or a call button on a landing panel, the system shall move the cabin to the requested floor.
FUN(02) The system shall accept multiple floor requests that are stored in a linked list implemented in C.
FUN(03) The system shall keep the doors closed while the cabin is moving.
FUN(04) The system shall keep the doors open for a sufficient time for passengers to enter or exit the cabin.
FUN(05) The system shall light each button when it is pressed and keep it lit until the request is served.
FUN(06) The system should ignore a floor request for the floor where the cabin is currently stopped.
FUN(07) When the alarm button is pressed, the system shall sound the alarm.
## 3.2 Performance requirements
PER(01) The system shall start moving the cabin within 2 seconds after the doors are closed.
PER(02) The system shall complete every trip within 1 second after the doors are closed.
## 3.7 Software system attributes QUA(01) The system shall move the cabin smoothly between floors.
# 5 Appendixes
## 5.1 Assumptions and dependencies
The system depends on the door operation, which is provided by ACME.
## 5.2 Acronyms and abbreviations
**ACME:** the manufacturer of the elevator.
**SRS:** Software Requirements Specification.
